utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar, ready for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, the next witness will be K72.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation which is shown to you on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sit down. Now, Mr. Behar has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Thank you very much for joining us here today. I know you've come a long way to be here. I'm going to begin by showing you a document that contains some personal information related to you. I'm going to indicate that this is 65 ter 02392. Can you please just read that document quietly to yourself, sir. Is the information on that document -- and that's your name and your date of -- and place of birth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that pseudonym sheet under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And just a reminder --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1322.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Just a reminder, sir, I'll be referring you to today as K72 in order to protect your identity. I understand, sir, that you are an ethnic Serb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did you complete any military service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell us when that took place?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what town you lived in in 19 -- pardon me, 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And as of 1999, how long have you lived in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Until June 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But prior to that how long had you lived in Djakovica? How many years had you been there up until that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: From 1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that after your military service, after you finished that, you began to work as an excavator; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And in order to do that you operated essentially a large excavating machine; is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Are you still doing that type of work today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell us how long you've been doing that work for? In other words, when did you begin and up to this point how long have you been working as an excavator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I've been doing that for around 30 years, 33 years in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you some questions, sir, about the work that you've done as an excavator. I'll have a number of questions about some different areas and if I can, I'd like to go slowly and step by step through the work that you've done. First, I understand you did some excavating work for the VJ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Court how that came about, in other words, how were you first hired or retained by the VJ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Sometime in 1998 one ranking officer approached me. He didn't tell me his name or anything, and he said that I should do some work for them digging trenches to dig in combat vehicles and similar work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you know or did you have a sense of that man's rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No, I don't think he had any rank insignia. He said he was a lieutenant-colonel. Now, whether that's true or not, I cannot know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Did you eventually do some work for the VJ then after he asked you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, I did a lot of work for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And what type of work did you do for the VJ? Can you explain that just briefly for the Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The thoroughfares used by the army below a ground level digging trenches in order to dig in military vehicles, that kind of thing. Digging bunkers as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And I wonder if just briefly, sir, could you explain the machine that you operate to the Judges and to the Court today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: A simple excavator, the kind you can see in the streets to this day. It has wheels.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Is it essentially a large digging machine; am I correct in that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And does it have a shovel on the front that you operate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us when it was that you worked for the VJ, roughly the time-period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: In 1998 before the bombing and during the bombing in 1999, the VJ and the police at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And were you paid by the VJ for that work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you explain how it was that you would be paid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I was paid cash. I would sign off on a list. The amount was very small. That's how I was paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And on a day-to-day basis, how would you know what type of work or what job you would be doing for the VJ on a particular day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I would never know in advance what I would be doing until I get there on site.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how would you know what site to go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They would take me there to show me what I needed to do. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So would they come to your house to pick you up in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, did you do any work for the MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: How did that come about that you first started working for the MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: It was the same as with the army. In peacetime I would work on roads for them a little less than for the army, and later on, an officer came to my house and told me that he was taking me to do some work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Is my understanding correct that you had already been doing some work for the VJ at that time and then a MUP officer came to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, I was working in a parallel for both of them as required.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And at the outset when you first started working for the MUP, what kind of work were you doing for them?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could all unnecessary typing please stop from the Office of the Prosecutor's desk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Roads, fortifications sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think we missed part of that answer, sir. I wonder if you could just repeat - I apologise for that - the type of work that you were doing for them. I know you mentioned roads and fortifications but perhaps if you could just --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I said roads. I know that they were targeted by sniping a great deal in some villages, and I was digging those roads below ground level that they could use and they had shields for cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And when you are talking about roads below ground level, are you referring to trenches; am I understanding that correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And with the MUP, how did you learn what kind of work you would be doing for them each day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I would not know until I got to my destination for that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Was it similar to your work for the VJ in that someone would typically come to your house to pick you up, or did it work differently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The same. A driver would come, pick me up, take me somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And were you paid for these jobs by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how would you be paid by the MUP typically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The same as with the army, cash.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you feel that you had a choice with respect to whether you could work for them or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No, I knew that I had to do it. The moment they came to pick me up, I knew I could not refuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you do any work for the local civilian protection or the local Territorial Defence at any point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And do you know who or what organisation you were working for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I think it was the civilian protection because the carcasses of dead animals which were killed during the bombing needed to be collected, so I buried them. I suppose that was the job of the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And is that primarily the work that did you for them, dealing with burying of dead animals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, that was the only work I did for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Do you remember what specific people, or can you identify some of the specific people you worked for in the local civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I remember because I knew these people from back at school. One was Matanovic whose first name I can't remember, and Rakovic. They would show me the locations, we would do the job the same day. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you have any interactions with the mayor of the town as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I know you've spoken to this Tribunal previously about your involvement with excavating some bodies. I want to ask you some detailed questions about that, and I'm going to try to go step by step if I can. Can you tell us how you were first contacted about this work that involved the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Sometime in the month of April, I think, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how were you first contacted in relation to these jobs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: One man in uniform came. He said he was an officer, but he was wearing no rank insignia, and he said we were going to perform a delicate job. He had come to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: This man in uniform, what organisation was he from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The police. He was wearing a police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And could you also describe for us what that uniform looked like, just in terms of colouring, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And roughly what time did he come to pick you up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Around 8.00 or 9.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this MUP officer took you, or where you went after he came to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: First we went to the police station. There I picked up my machine and then we headed for Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: By machine you mean your excavator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Am I understanding right that was kept off site then? Where would you normally keep your excavator, or were there different excavators you would use?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: There were several places where I could park, and I had only one excavator at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So you mentioned that you headed for Prizren, towards Prizren. Where did you go exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: We turned off just before Bistrazin, perhaps 100 metres before Bistrazin, we turned off the road. The place, the destination was 100 metres away perhaps from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you explain to us how you drove there exactly. In other words, were you driving the excavator, and where was the MUP officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I drove my excavator to that place, and that man showed me the location and then drove back to the road. He showed me what I needed to do, where I needed to dig, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I'll come to those details in a moment. When you are driving, you mentioned he drove, is he in a different car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: What kind of vehicle was that that he was driving in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: A passenger car. I don't remember what make. A police car.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Just so we are clear, is it a marked police car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly whether it was marked police. They had civilian cars and marked police cars. I can't remember exactly what that one was like.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you, sir. Can you tell us what you saw when you arrived at the site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I had seen that some digging had been done there already. There was a strong stench, and I felt straightaway that corpses must be involved and then I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell us what this area was like generally that you were brought to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: It was a clearing, a bit sandy, 100 metres away from the road. A clearing, level ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Were you asked to do something once you had arrived at the site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, I was told to start digging. That's what he told me to do. I started digging and then I saw what was beneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you explain exactly what you did, what type of digging and what that involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I excavated human bodies. There were four or five gypsies around. They would separate the bodies up to the point where I could reach with my shovel and from there they would pick the bodies up and throw them into the refrigerator truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe what you saw -- I'm referring to the bodies that you've described. Can you describe these bodies and what you could see as you were excavating them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, I could see that the gypsies searched the pockets. They would take whatever they found, a little ring, a chain with a locket. I damaged many of the bodies with the machine. They were not particularly badly mutilated, but it happens with an excavator, you will detach an arm, a leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Could you tell what gender the bodies were that you were pulling up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And could you tell what they were wearing in terms of clothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And what sort of condition were the bodies in? And what I mean by that is could you tell how much they had decomposed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Not much. There was just this terrible stench. I cannot judge how long they had been in the ground. They were not in the state of decomposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Were you able to see their faces and make out the faces of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: It was very difficult. They were covered with earth and sand. I could only discern them to a certain extent, but not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, did your excavator have a light on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And was that on as you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Only short headlights, and that was done because the bombing was in progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Do you know how many bodies you dug up at that site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I don't know. I had been told that there were some hundred odd bodies. I didn't count them and if I give you any figure, I may be mistaken, but I had been told that there were some hundred bodies there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you were told that? Who told you and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: A police officer told me after I'd asked him when is this going to end, and he said very soon. There were about 100 bodies, but I don't know if the information he gave me was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And after you unearthed these bodies then, can you explain to us where you would put them with the excavator, and what happened after you pulled them out of the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: These gypsies were first loading them into a refrigerator truck and a small truck as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe those trucks for us, the refrigerated truck and the smaller truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The refrigerator truck was a small ordinary one that you see every day on the roads. Both the ordinary truck and the refrigerator truck were small. They were some 15 metres away from me and due to the poor lighting, I couldn't see exactly what they were doing. I just know that they were loading the bodies. I put them about 5 or 6 metres from my excavator and then they would take them and load them into the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did those trucks have licence plates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I didn't see any. I don't think they had, but I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Do you remember what colour the refrigerator truck was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I know that the box was white. I mean, that's the usual colour of these type of trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how long were you unearthing these bodies for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: About two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you describe what your feeling or your reaction was as you were doing this job for those two or three hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: It was harrowing. What else could it have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: While you were doing this job, sir, can you describe who else was at the scene besides you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Only myself and the people who were loading the body, and the police security officer and a few vehicles were some 20 or 30 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Were there other police there generally on the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No, not on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And you mentioned vehicles, I think, slightly farther away. Can you explain who was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The policemen were there, but on the very spot where we were working there was this terrible stench and due to that, no one was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: These policemen who are farther away, can you explain what they are doing there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, they were standing and waiting. I don't know what they were doing. It was night. I just had my short lights and I could only see them standing there, but I don't know what they were doing in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: How many police officers were there approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I can only guess. There were two, three, or four vehicles, but how many of them were in the vehicles, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us as well what the police on the scene were wearing in terms of clothing or a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were wearing blue camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: What happened when you finished the work on the scene that you had been asked to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I drove the machine back and went home. Well, actually, they drove me home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And by they, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The police. I was driven home in a police car.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you get paid for this job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: You mean that particular job that I did on that day?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, that job on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No, no, no. I suppose I did something else during the day so they probably combined everything that I did on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand, sir, you were also involved in an event in Brekovac outside of Djakovica or Gjakove, I'd like to ask you some questions about that. Can you tell us first when it was that that event took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Perhaps some 20 days after this event that I just described, I don't remember the exact date. I don't remember actually no date, so I would say 15 or 20 days give or take after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell us how you became involved in this second event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Like before, one day they came and told me let's go into a job. My excavator was parked at the time by an elementary school. It was in a completely different location. I was told to come along and do a job. Again I didn't know what I was going to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And if I can just break that down a little bit. You said one day they came and told you to do a job. Can you explain who it was who came there to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, the police again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Was it the same person as before or someone different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: It was a different person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how was this police officer dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: In a camouflage blue uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did he come in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And what type of vehicle was it? Was that a police vehicle, or do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I think it was again a police car, passenger car, but I don't know the make.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you know this police officer? Had you known him from before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened after you left your house with this officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: We drove to the school where my excavator was parked. We didn't set off immediately because he told me we had to wait for awhile until nightfall, and that's when we went to Brekovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did he tell you why you needed to wait until nightfall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: The type of work that you were doing, would this be easier work to do during the day or at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Of course it's easier to do it during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So after it was dark and you set out, can you explain where you went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: We went to the cemetery in Brekovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell us again how you drove there exactly? Were you driving your excavator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how was he driving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: In the same car that had taken us from my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right. And was he driving in front of you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Do you remember where in town this cemetery was located, just approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: All I know is that it was 2, 3, maybe 5 kilometres from the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Are you aware of a barracks in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: How far was it from there, roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I know it's nearby but I wouldn't like to guess. It seemed to me 3, 4, or 5 kilometres from the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And do you know whose barracks those were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The barracks of the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: When you arrived at the site, sir, what were you -- what were you told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I was told to enter the cemetery with my excavator. There was quite a wide driveway through it, and to start digging individual graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And when you say "digging individual graves," do you mean digging a hole or digging something up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: People had already been buried there, and I was told to dig them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what those graves looked like when you got there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were individual graves with a mound of earth. There was a plank there bearing a name, not all of them, but quite a few of them had names on these kind of planks, upright planks. Some had names written on them, some didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did you see what types of names were written on those planks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were all males.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And were you able to tell the types of names in terms of ethnicity, what types of males those were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I suppose that they were Muslims judging by the name, but that may not necessarily be true. I did assume that they were Muslims though.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And could you tell or did you have a sense if these were recent graves or if they had been there for longer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were recent. They hadn't been there for long.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And are you able to say what makes you think that, how you reach that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, judging by the soil, it was fresh, and that told me that it hadn't been there for long.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what you did at the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I took those bodies one by one. There were gypsies again who were loading them on a tractor-trailer and a big truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe that larger truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: It was a tractor-trailer. I couldn't see how big it was, and it couldn't enter the cemetery. It had a tarpaulin on it and for that reason the bodies had to be taken out of the cemetery compound on a tractor-trailer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So was it a two-stage process then? Were they loading the smaller tractor-trailer first and then loading the larger truck from there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You mentioned there were gypsies who were loading the bodies. Did you recognise any of these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Maybe two of them in the previous team who worked on the previous location. Possibly two of them. At least that's what I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how many of these gypsies that you've described were there at the scene, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: There were five or six of them, or maybe four. Two of them were loading the bodies on to the tractor and two of them were loading them on to the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: How long did you spend at this job pulling bodies from the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, if we started it around 10.00 or 9.00 in the evening, we finished at about 10.00 the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Do you have a sense of how many bodies you pulled from the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No. I cannot guess. There were quite a few of them, but I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Would you say it was more than the previous job in Bistrazin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe the bodies, what they looked like in this job as you were pulling them out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They hadn't been in the ground for long. One could discern faces here and there. Some of them were naked to the waist, they had shot wounds. Some of the bodies I damaged again with my excavator, so it was a tough job.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Were you able to tell the gender? Were the bodies male or female?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were all males.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you describe the clothing, the type of clothing that they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were in civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I believe you had previous at one point described seeing a marking of the KLA on one of the bodies. Are you able to describe that for the Court, what that looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, yes. If they were in uniforms, they would put it on over the civilian clothes and if they realised that they were in danger, they would discard their uniform and remain in their civilian clothes. One of them had his head shaven in such a way that it made the letters UCK.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, that last part is what I was referring to. Was that the only such marking, the only KLA or UCK marking that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: That's the only one I noticed. Whether there were any other, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe the police presence at the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I didn't know any of them. They only had blue camouflage uniforms without any insignia or rank patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how many police were at the scene, roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were again far away from me. Nobody was on the spot. They were just securing the area. I can't give you the number. Maybe 10, 15, 20. I can't give you any number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe, sir, what the truck looked like, the final truck once all the bodies had been loaded into it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: It was far away from me, but I saw that it was a truck trailer with tarpaulin and I saw them loading the bodies into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Once the bodies had been fully loaded, were you able to see them then on the truck, or were they covered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: When did the truck leave the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: As soon as everything was finished, the truck left before I did. I stayed awhile to flatten the earth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, maybe I just want to clarify something. When I asked you previously about the gentleman or the body that you saw with the UCK shaved in the head, you had said something previously that says: "If they were in uniforms they would put it on over the civilian clothes. If they realised they were in danger, then they would discard their uniform and remain in their civilian clothes." I just want to be clear, that's not something that you saw, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djordjevic? A leading question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just first get a reference for what my learned friend is saying so the Defence can check that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I apologise. I thank my friend for pointing that out. It's at page 19 of the transcript at line 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, sir, I just want to make sure I'm not misled by that. Did you see any people putting on civilian clothes or discarding a uniform at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No, I did not see that, but I saw quite often around Djakovica whenever I went to work on locations, I saw discarded uniforms, and I heard while I was around army people that that was their tactics, but I can't say that I personally saw them taking off uniforms, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And just focusing on the observations then that you made at the scene, did you see any uniforms at the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No. No, it was night, and I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Let me return, then, you described the truck leaving the scene. I believe you described leaving the scene yourself. After you left the scene, did you go to a gas station to fill your machine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe where that gas station was located roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: To the right of the Djakovica-Prizren road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe what, if anything, happened when you were at the gas station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Nothing happened, just the man working at the gas station asked me if I was the one who had loaded that truck ahead of me, and I said no, I had no clue, I had just set out from my house to do some work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Was he aware the contents of the truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Maybe he didn't know. Maybe he could just feel the horrible stench and made an inference, but he couldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did he say anything about bodies then, when you say make an inference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: As soon as I stopped, he told me, Did you load that tractor-trailer that just passed? The stench is horrible, I suppose it must be corpses. I said no, I had no idea what that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I understand you were also involved in another operation in Guska to the west of Djakovica. Can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Not long after the one in Brekovac, a day or two later. It might even have been the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you ended up doing that job? Let me be clear, can you tell us how you ended up being involved on this Guska job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Again a uniformed man came to pick me up to take me to do some work. I collected my excavator, he led the way, I followed him, and we went to Guska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And just so we are clear, I know you've said "uniformed man," and what organisation was this man with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: A blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And what organisation was he with, just so we are clear, sir, in court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So you've described him again leading the way much like last time, you were driving behind him in the excavator then again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Where did he take you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The settlement called Guska. Perhaps a little outside the settlement itself. I had never been there before. We came to a feature of some kind. I was not familiar with it, and that's where I needed to dig up something.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe that feature that you are referring to where you stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: It's very vague in my memory. I know it was a low building. It was certainly not a residential building, perhaps a place of worship of some kind. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And what were you asked to do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: In three rows there were three or four graves per row, I was supposed to dig them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And once you had pulled the bodies up with your machine, what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were loaded on to a smaller truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And again, did anyone assist with that loading process?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The gypsies again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe what that truck looked like, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I don't remember. I can only remember it was small. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And are you able to describe what the graves looked like in more detail?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were unmarked, I think. There was a small mound of earth on each, in three rows. Ordinary graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And when you pulled the bodies out, were there single bodies in each grave, was there more than one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Right next to this place there were small -- there was a small wooded area, and there would be two bodies in one grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I'll come to that in a moment, but so for these first graves you were digging, they were individual graves; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And the bodies that you were pulling out from these graves, are you able to describe them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Do you recall if they were male or female?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Male. All of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And do you recall the clothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you have a sense of the recency of the burial, whether it was fairly recent or if they been there for longer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: To be honest, I never gave it much thought. Perhaps they had not been there a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: What happened then after you finished unearthing those bodies and they had been loaded into the truck? I think you mentioned another area. What happened when you completed that part of the job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Then we moved to the other area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you describe this other area? First, how far was it from the first area you had been digging in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: It was not very far away. It was some kind of woods. That was the second site.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And when you say "woods," can you describe what the vegetation was like? Are we talking about trees, are we talking about something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No, no, not trees. Underbrush perhaps because I was be able to move over it in my excavator.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And what did you do in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The same thing, digging up bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you describe where the bodies were within that area? In other words, were they mostly in one place, were they dispersed, can you explain that to the Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were not disturbed, but they were not all centred in one spot. They were scattered about a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: How did you know where the bodies were and where to dig?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: There was a uniformed policeman with me who shone a flash-light to show me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Would he shine the flash-light on a grave to show you to dig in that place; am I understanding that correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the police presence was at the scene? How many police were there, roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Again roughly, I don't know. Perhaps ten. But you can't take my word for it. They were rather far away from me. It was a remote place. You wouldn't want me to guess, would you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: No, we wouldn't, sir. I appreciate that. Aside from the officer who was guiding you directly, did you have a sense of what the other officers were doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I can't say even roughly because we were never there together on the site. They would stand away from me while I was doing the job, and then I was the last to leave the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Again, sir, the bodies that you were digging up in this area, are you able to describe those bodies? First, were they male or female?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were all men. I think one body was in the Turkish pantaloon type of trousers, but I think that one was a man too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: What type of clothing were they wearing more generally? Were they wearing civilian clothes, were they uniformed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Civilian, civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Were you able to tell the age of any of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No, no, that would be difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I know I didn't really ask you that with respect to some of the other bodies you unearthed, but were you able generally to tell with these bodies that you were digging up what age they would be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I know they were all adults. Faces would be covered with soil. It was night-time, the lighting was poor. It would be very difficult to judge their age, but I know they were all adults.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And with respect to this site, what was your -- did you have a sense of the ethnicity of these bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: There was nothing -- no marking on the graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, with respect to all three of these operations that you worked on what your sense was of how organised the operations were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They were badly organised. That much I know. It's something that shouldn't have happened, but once it did, the traces remained. Many many traces. So the next day everybody would be able to see what had gone on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did they appear preplanned to you, sir, these operations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I don't know about planning. I can't know that. I just know it was badly done, all of it. Something was being covered up, but I cannot tell you more. I just had my job with a machine, with an excavator, whether you do digging here or digging there. Nor would anyone tell me about any plan, so I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You say "something was being covered up," are you able to explain that, why you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, the fact that it was all done after nightfall. It was all done by night, and these were jobs that would, of course, have been much easier in daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And at the end of this -- the third exhumation that you described in Guska, were you spoken to by anyone from the MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, one man kind of threatened me and he said that I could lose my life if I talk about that. I don't know the man either. He was also in a blue uniform, no insignia. And I answered that I had already told my wife, which was true, she knew about every job I did. And I also said I had told a lawyer. He did put a bit of fright into me, but it's not true that I had spoken to a lawyer at the time. I had just spoken to my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you explain to us why you told him that you had spoken to a lawyer and why you told him that you had spoken to your wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I said that I had told my wife because I was scared. It's not like I didn't care. I thought something might happen to me all of a sudden. And that's why I told him I had spoken to a lawyer and told him the story, and if anything happens to me, it will come out. But it's not true. I had not spoken to any lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Were you worried at that time that something might happen to you, and can you explain why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: There was no time to really get scared. I wasn't that scared. It was an awful time anyway, the bombing and everything. I did worry a bit that somebody could eliminate me. He did not make that threat in so many words. He told me that I could lose my head if I talked too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand, just so we are clear, just the last line here. You said: "He did not make that threat in so many words, but he told me that I could lose my head if I talked too much." That first threat that you could lose your head if you talked too much, did he say that directly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in those words. I could see that he was trying to hide something but that's -- there was a big job, many people were involved. You could not hide that kind of thing. That was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right. So the threat that you are saying he didn't make in so many words was this other threat you just described that somebody could eliminate you regardless; am I understanding that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No, that's something that went through my head. He didn't say that someone could eliminate me. He just said that I could lose my head if I talk around.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. I think we are clear. Just a couple of other brief areas I wanted to ask you about before I conclude. Did you have any involvement in relation to NATO bombs that hit a convoy of Kosovo Albanian refugees near the Bistrazin bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell us how you ended up being involved in that, how it came about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: That bomb hit the column of people and damaged the road badly. It was the Djakovica-Prizren road. So the MUP sent me again to repair the road, to fill that hole in the ground with gravel and earth, and that's how I came to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Once you were there, did you end up dealing with some of the Albanians on scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, there were some people waiting for me there. They asked me to transfer a couple of bodies in the shovel of my excavator across the bridge to Bistrazin so that they can be buried there. I accepted, and I moved those bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So were you essentially just carrying them then in the shovel of your machine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And were they loading them then into your machine and you drove them across; am I understanding that correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the MUP aware that you were -- that you had done that as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did they say anything to you about that, speak to you about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They advised me not to go to the other side of the bridge because there was no police presence there, that I would be in danger, that those people would kill me. But I did transfer those bodies. I did not go up to their village. They -- just across the bridge they took the bodies over, put them on to some sort of smaller machine, and I went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Could I have up 65 ter 00035, please. Just have a couple of more minutes, Your Honours. I think I'll be finished shortly. Your Honours, perhaps we should just briefly have the -- or just have a break, and I'll just have a couple of short questions afterwards. Perhaps it's a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Behar. We will have the first break now and resume at 11.00. A Court Officer will assist you during the break, and we'll carry on in half an hour's time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, there are just a few areas I wanted to briefly revisit with you. The gas station that you described going to after the Brekovac job, can you tell us who that gas station was run by? Are you receiving translation, sir? No. Just a moment then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you had better repeat the question, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I'll just ask the question again. The gas station that you described going to after the job you did in Brekovac, can you tell us who that gas station was run by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The police filled the tank or actually I always used to fill my tank there. The company that owned it was a socially-owned company, and I never paid for the petrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So when you say "the police filled the tank," was it a MUP gas station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I don't believe that it was theirs. This gas station used to exist before that as a socially-owned gas station. They were just using it, and I never paid for the petrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And when you say you never paid for the petrol, was that because you were doing work for the MUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I suppose so. Who would otherwise give me petrol free -- for free?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And so they the ability to do that at that gas station then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't put it that way. I don't know what the arrangement was and who made this arrangement for the petrol supply. There were other petrol stations, but they were demolished by the bombing. As I said, I don't know what the arrangement was for the use of this particular petrol station.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, on the three jobs you described doing that involved bodies, do you know where the police who you saw there at the scene were sent from? In other words, do you know if they were local police or if they had come from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I didn't know them. I don't know where they came from or who had sent them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you recognise any of the policemen individually as being from Djakovica or from anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No, not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to the unearthing of these bodies, you said previously, this is at page 28, line 17, you said that these were big jobs and many people were involved. I want to ask, based on your experience working for the MUP on a number of jobs, at what level do you think that such operations were authorised?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There's a lot of typing coming from the Prosecution desk, and it's disturbing for the interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there was an authorisation, it must have come from a higher level. This is at least what I think. I never heard anything of the sort from anyone. Nobody mentioned any specific name. Therefore, I cannot say for certainty, and I can't imagine who would say such a thing to me or to a regular police officer. Since this was a considerable job, it must have been ordered from a high level, but this is just my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can I ask you, sir, with respect to the first job you described, that was digging in the Bistrazin area, can you explain to us how exactly the area was secured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Just like during any other work that I was involved in, it was secured by the police, so no access was allowed to anyone. That's how they secured the area. Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you see if there was a perimeter set up or if roads were blocked, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The road was blocked, whereas on the other side there was no need for that. There was a river. Even if there had been some security officer posted there, I hadn't seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And what about with respect to the third job you described in Guska with respect to how that area was secured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The same thing. There were policemen there, I don't know how many of them. They were moving around with torches, but I don't know exactly what the arrangements were. It was night and one couldn't see particularly well what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Were you able to see if there were any roadblocks or a particular perimeter set up on that job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: There was some form of security. As for the road traffic, I don't know whether the road was closed. I did see some vehicles passing by but they could have been MUP vehicles. I think that the road was secured at that time. Whereas in the woods, there was no need for any such arrangements.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If I could have you look at the screen now, there's map in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Perhaps we could just have that zoomed in around the Djakovica area. And perhaps just scroll down slightly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I just wanted to ask you briefly if you could mark on the map the three locations that you described digging in, and I'll take you through them one by one. If you can just use that pen. Before you start, sir, can you first mark the Bistrazin area. Do you see Bistrazin on there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Can I just have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: We might even be able to zoom in just slightly more, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If you could just draw a circle around that area and mark it with a 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you also mark Brekovac. Do you see that on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you mark that with a 2, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And finally if could you mark Guska. Again circle it and perhaps you could indicate a number 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, those are --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1323, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, those are my questions for you. Thank you very much for your patience. And my learned friend from the Defence will have some questions for you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Behar. Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, K72. My name is Dragoljub Djordjevic, Defence counsel for the accused, the former police general Vlastimir Djordjevic. Ms. Marie O'Leary is my legal assistant and part of our team. Mr. K72, since we both speak the same language and you already have some experience when you gave evidence in the Milutinovic case, I would kindly ask you to wait until I have finished my question and after it has been translated in order to allow the interpreters to do their job properly, and I'm going to follow the same procedure as well. In view of what we have heard here today, I will definitely have a considerably shorter cross-examination for you than the one that I had originally anticipated. First of all, K72, when did you actually have a contact with the investigators from this Tribunal? When did that actually take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Sometime in 2005 or 2006, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: How did that come about, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I received an invitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: There was this organisation, I don't remember its name. I was asked to come to Belgrade where the investigators from the Tribunal were. Mr. Paolo or something. We had an interview there then I received summons from the district court saying that some people from BIA were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of the organisation that called you? How did they get in touch with you? Where were you living at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Where I'm still living.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Outside of Kosovo, that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, how did they find you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone ask you anything about that you were supposed to testify? Did anyone explain how they learned about you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They told me that they had a witness who knew about my work who was there while I was doing my work. Nobody was mentioned in terms of indictment. They just spoke about the work that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that you did your military service in 1971 in Batajnica, that you were an aviation mechanic, and that after you left the army you started to work as an excavator operator for a company. Can you tell me where were you trained as an operator? What actually is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly requested to wait for the questions and answers to be finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Where were you trained to operate this particular construction machine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: In the Dunav-Tisa-Dunav Canal Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you couldn't get a job immediately, you first had to undergo certain training for an operator on this particular construction machine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You started working immediately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, your questions are coming too quickly for the interpreters. There needs to be a pause between the answer of the witness and your next question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to admit that I will do my best to comply but this is totally in contrary to my temperament.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You started working there and then you went to Djakovica. Why did you actually go to Djakovica? I think you said it was in 1998. Why did you go to Djakovica? What prompted you to go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: My company was working on an irrigation system for five or six years. I got married there, and I remained living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, what is the ethnicity of your wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: She's a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is her educational background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: She has finished secondary school of economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Was she employed there in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: For how long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Until 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You have two children; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did your children attend school in Djakovica until 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The older daughter did but the younger one was only one year old at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since your company probably finished this irrigation system in Djakovica, what did you do then after the works were completed and your company suspended operations in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I remained in Djakovica, but I still continued to work for the same company.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: How was that possible? What job did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I also operated an excavator, and we worked according to a special schedule. We would work for two weeks and then we had two weeks off when I went to Novi Sad, and after that I would go back to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any property in Djakovica? Where did you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: We rented a flat. After that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption, Your Honour, but I wonder if we should be pursuing these matters in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I assumed this was a private session from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, it's entirely a public session with the witness's identity being withheld.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I would kindly ask for us to move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that would be a wise precaution. Yes, private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: This remuneration that you received for the work you did when you worked, tell me, you were in Djakovica throughout the whole period of the bombing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, I did receive it during the bombing, but not every time. I received these so-called daily allowances, sometimes on the MUP premises, sometimes elsewhere because the MUP had actually moved to some houses, and I was paid sometimes in one of those houses. It was paid to me on a fortnightly basis and according to the number of actual working days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We have resolved one dilemma that both the OTP and I had so far, when you said that you were paid by the police, you said that you received this money from the treasurer. In all your previous statements that remained unclear. This time you specifically said from the treasurer. Does that mean that the same applied to the army, that you also received money from the treasurer and signed the papers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, the same applied to the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: So it was a treasurer who paid you, not some mysterious person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Well, I say a treasurer, but this person was in a uniform, and he carried money in a brief-case. But I don't know whether he did the job of a treasurer or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I think it was only normal for him to be in uniform, whether he be a policeman or a serviceman, but I think for the first time you mentioned today the treasurer's office; is that right? You never said that before.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I was referring to the treasurer, the person who pays the money. I don't know if he did some other job, whether he was a driver or whatever, but that was the person who gave me the money, and I considered him to be a treasurer. That could not have been the case though.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other citizens in Djakovica who were paid by the police on the same principles for the work they did? For example, the gypsies that you said helped you during the exhumation of the remains at these three locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: All those who did some work were paid in the same way. There were a lot of truck drivers who drove construction material for building covers and centres, but I wasn't interested in details. All of them were engaged, but they were dressed in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: This question that I just asked you was already put to you. Actually, I put it to you because I wanted to clarify whether you were the only one who exclusively received 10 German marks during the war or not. Now I understand that there were other people in the same position. All right. That's it. Now, I asked you, but you never gave me an answer, about the bombing of Djakovica. In view of the nature of the job that you did, you were operating a construction machine, what can you tell me about that? Do you know which targets were bombed, if you know? Let's start with that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: A lot of military facilities were bombed including barracks, then the police administration building and station, sometimes private houses and petrol stations, maybe some other facilities, but I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is quite sufficient. Tell me, is it fair to say that there were over 100 assaults and air-strikes between the 24th of March and June 1999 when you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: There were much more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Did you take part in clearing the rubble in some situations relating to the bombing of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any casualties among the army personnel and policemen during the bombing that at least you yourself could see or heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The so-called Minaj [phoen] settlement was totally demolished, and I went there to clear up the rubble. The column was targeted travelling along the road. That was it, I don't remember any other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: This settlement that you mentioned was a civilian residential area, not a military facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, it was a civilian residential area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any casualties there as a result of the bombing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: There were two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I understand that you cannot remember when the column of the Albanian refugees was bombed in the vicinity of Bistrazin, but in spite of that, could you try and remember relative to the work that you did in unearthing the grave-site in Bistrazin, when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to bother you with this any longer. Tell me now, was the Cabrat barracks bombed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Where I was, there were only tents. That was not the proper barracks, but it was bombed. Military and combat equipment were entrenched there and there were communications as well there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that you received payment from the army at Cabrat. You also told us that this site was bombed and eventually destroyed. Does that mean that later on you received remuneration or that it was actually possible -- or actually where it was possible but not where you said that you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: The army paid me out at several locations, this so-called remuneration.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: So it was possible and feasible during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That applies to the police as well, when the police station in Djakovica was destroyed at the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the machine for which you claim to have been parked outside the police station, that you always picked up there, actually means that you went elsewhere where the police was to pick up the machine, not at the police station, given that the state of war was proclaimed so nobody would leave the machine there for it to be destroyed by the bombing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I used to leave my machine after I had finished my job to the nearest location to my home. I can't remember now how many locations I used. If it was needed for the army, they would tell me leave it there. If it was required for the needs of the Territorial Defence, they would tell me where to leave it. This is how it worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's a fair answer because what we heard so far before in the Milutinovic case and in your statements as well was totally illogical, and it sounded as if there had never been a war in Djakovica. You said that after the war you left Djakovica, and you said that you were on good terms with Albanians and that you still maintained contact with some of them to this date, but you left, nevertheless. What was the reason? Did any of the Serbs and other non-Albanians remain in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Maybe three or four elderly Serbs stayed behind. I personally left not because I was afraid of my neighbours, but because I was afraid of some other people unknown to me. That was the reason why I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Even though immediately thereafter international forces were deployed there with a mandate of keeping peace and good relations, inter-ethnic relations in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: I didn't wait for them to arrive. I left before that. I think it was the 12th or the 13th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Was the reason for your leaving your permanent engagement by the army and the police during the war? Were you afraid because of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes, very much so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to the bombing of the refugee column of Albanians. I don't remember the exact date when it happened but what is important is the following: You went to the scene. Who told you to go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Somebody from the police. I don't know exactly who.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: So you went there, helped with resolving the situation, you even helped some other people to carry the dead bodies and hand them over to the Albanians. Did you notice any police on the scene, and were they helping the wounded, women and children from the column? I'm talking about the policemen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: They gave them some food from their own rations. That much I was able to see. I didn't see any wounded people. There were five or six of them whom I carried across the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: But those were the dead people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K72
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
